name: Outreach
tagline: Sales engagement platform with sequence automation and analytics.
description: Outreach is a sales engagement platform for building sequences, dialing prospects, and reading how each step of a campaign performs.
pros: Sequences mix email, call, and task steps and keep running without the rep re-planning each individual touch
A dialer sits inside the platform, so calling belongs to the sequence instead of becoming a detour to a separate system
Step-level analytics show where a cadence loses replies — a question a shared mailbox cannot answer
Deal and pipeline analytics re-read execution data to comment on revenue rather than only on sends
The band this repository records, $100-250/mo, gives a buyer a starting figure before contacting the vendor
cons: Sequences require an owner: someone must design the steps, keep them current, and retire the ones that stop earning replies
The platform assumes a CRM exists elsewhere, so an organization with no record system buys two systems to obtain one workflow
Certification, retention schedule, and residency terms are all absent from this repository's fields for Outreach

features.description: Dials prospects from the engagement workspace and returns call activity to the sequence. Number coverage and recording rules are not itemized.

features.name: Email and sequence analytics
features.description: Open, click, and reply measurement at step and sequence level. Report types and history windows are not listed in this dataset.

features.name: Deal and pipeline analytics
features.description: Reads execution activity alongside pipeline to flag movement and risk. The individual signals available are not enumerated in this repository.

features.name: Rep task and inbox queue
features.description: Surfaces the day's next actions so reps work from a queue rather than from a plan they maintain. Triage behavior is not documented here.

features.name: CRM synchronization
features.description: Keeps contacts, accounts, and outcomes aligned with the system of record. Named CRM partners are not listed in this dataset.

features.name: Webhooks and REST endpoints
features.description: Programmatic access for moving activity and record data between systems. Endpoint coverage and limits are not recorded here.

content.title: Outreach as a sequence engine
content.body: Outreach is a sales engagement platform: it does not hold the customer record, it executes the touches that go onto one. Teams build sequences — ordered steps of email, calls, and tasks — and Outreach runs them across a list of prospects, keeping each rep's day supplied with the next action. This repository's descriptor for the product is a sales engagement platform with sequence automation and analytics, recorded under CRM & Sales with a paid model and a band of $100-250/mo. The category guidance stored here draws the boundary plainly: a CRM answers what is happening, while platforms like Outreach answer how to execute.

content.title: Steps, cadences, and the built-in dialer
content.body: A sequence is a script with a schedule. Steps fire in order, stop when a prospect replies, and hand the rep a task when a person is required. Alongside that sits a dialer, so calling is not a detour out to a separate telephony tool, and call activity writes back to the sequence that prompted it. The catalog of step types and their conditions is where most of the product's power sits, and it is also where the administration lives — every rule a manager writes becomes a rule that governs a rep's day, which is a reason to design sequences as carefully as the messaging inside them.

content.title: Reading the sequence analytics
content.body: Sequence analytics answer questions no single mailbox can see, which is why they are the reporting surface this category is bought for. This repository's category file points at that surface directly, describing sales engagement platforms as tracking email opens, clicks, and call activity. What the dataset does not itemize for Outreach is which of the reports below actually ship, what the export formats are, or how far back history runs, so the list is a starting point for a vendor checklist rather than a confirmed inventory.
items: Open, click, and reply counts measured at each step
The step where a sequence most often loses a reply
Output compared across reps and across weeks
Call activity returned from the dialer into the sequence
Replies routed back so a sequence stops when a person answers

content.title: The revenue intelligence layer on top
content.body: Above the sequences sits a layer that treats deals and pipeline as the object of analysis: opportunity movement, signals about which deals are stalling, and coaching inputs drawn from recorded activity. That layer is what separates an engagement platform from an email-sending tool, because the same execution data is re-read to say something about revenue. The category notes stored in this repository describe revenue intelligence as capturing activity automatically and identifying at-risk deals, which is the framing in which Outreach's analytics sit. The dataset does not enumerate the individual signals or the models behind them.

content.title: Where the orchestration stops
content.body: Orchestration has a price that shows up organizationally rather than in the interface. Sequences and rules need an owner: someone to design the steps, keep them compliant, and retire the ones that stop working, which amounts to a part-time administrator at minimum. Outreach also assumes a CRM holds the record elsewhere, so a team without one is buying two systems. And because execution data is the raw material for every report the platform produces, the analytics are only as good as the rollout — a team that runs half its conversations through Outreach reads conclusions built on the other half.

content.title: The $100-250/mo record and what it hides
content.body: The band held for Outreach in this dataset is $100-250/mo under a paid pricing model, the highest entry figure among the engagement and pipeline tools this repository compares it against apart from the suite platforms. The field does not capture whether the band is per user, what telephony costs, or which analytics sit behind higher tiers. The comparison records quote the same band when weighing Outreach against Close CRM and Salesloft, each carried at its own recorded band — useful context even though none of the figures is a quote. Ask the vendor for its current published list before budgeting.

content.title: CRM sync and the system-of-record split
content.body: Outreach sits downstream of a system of record: contacts, accounts, and opportunities are synchronized from a CRM, executed on in Outreach, and written back. This repository's category guidance makes the arrangement explicit, describing many organizations as running a CRM as the system of record and an engagement platform as the system of action, integrated together — and it notes that major CRMs are adding native engagement features, which is the strategic pressure standing over standalone tools in this category. Named connectors are not itemized here; the comparison files show Outreach measured against Pipedrive, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho CRM, Close CRM, Copper CRM, Freshsales, Zendesk, and Salesloft.

content.title: Deployment, data path, and the missing certifications
content.body: Outreach runs as a hosted service: sequences, recordings, and analytics live in the vendor's infrastructure, which is what lets a team run the same cadence from laptops and phones. The dataset carries nothing further on this product's security posture — no certification, no retention schedule, no residency option, no identity-policy detail — and a hosted delivery model implies none of them. Call recordings and reply threads are among the more sensitive material a revenue team holds, so this is a gap to close with vendor documentation before procurement rather than after it.

content.title: Outreach against Salesloft and the CRM field
content.body: The closest recorded counterpart is Salesloft: the same category, 4.3/5 against Outreach's 4.2/5, and a band below the $100-250/mo held here. The emphasis this repository records differs — Salesloft as a platform for enterprise revenue teams with coaching and forecasting at the center, Outreach as sequence automation and analytics — which reads as a manager-facing product against an execution-facing one. Below that pair sit the CRMs, Pipedrive, Close CRM, Zoho CRM, HubSpot, and Salesforce, which own the record instead of the sequence.

content.title: Who runs Outreach, and the basis for this page
content.body: Outreach fits revenue teams whose problem is execution volume: a defined book of accounts, a known set of touches, and a need to see which touches work. It suits organizations that already own a CRM and want the outbound machinery beside it, and managers who intend to coach from activity data rather than from memory. It fits poorly as a first system for a company with no CRM, poorly for teams too small to maintain sequences, and poorly where the budget cannot absorb a band recorded at $100-250/mo. What is written here comes from vendor documentation and the comparison and category records this repository holds for Outreach.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Outreach and a CRM?
faqs.answer: A CRM holds contacts, accounts, and deals; Outreach executes sequenced touches on top of them. This repository's category notes describe the pair as system of record and system of action, usually integrated together.

faqs.question: How does Outreach differ from Salesloft?
faqs.answer: Both are engagement platforms here. Outreach is filed as sequence automation and analytics at $100-250/mo with 4.2/5; Salesloft as a platform for enterprise revenue teams, carried at a lower band, with 4.3/5 emphasizing coaching and forecasting.

faqs.question: Does Outreach include a dialer?
faqs.answer: Yes, calling sits inside the platform so dial activity returns to the sequence. Number provisioning, recording, and coverage details are not recorded in this repository.

faqs.question: What does our dataset say about Outreach pricing?
faqs.answer: A paid model with a band of $100-250/mo. Whether that is per seat, and what telephony or advanced analytics cost beyond it, is not captured — use the vendor’s published price list instead.

faqs.question: Are security certifications recorded for Outreach?
faqs.answer: No. Nothing in the certification, retention, residency, or identity fields for Outreach here, so those questions must go to the vendor's current documentation.

author: Sarah Chen
learningCurve: Sequences are quick to grasp; designing step logic, keeping analytics clean, and administering the platform is where the real work sits.
whoShouldUse: Revenue teams with a defined outbound motion and a CRM already in place, organizations that push real volume through sequenced email and calling, and managers who intend to coach from activity data.
whoShouldNotUse: Companies without a system of record to sync against, teams too small to own and maintain sequence logic, and buyers whose budget cannot cover a band this repository records at $100-250/mo.
